issue.body:
### Problem

`wacli sync --follow` holds the store lock for its full lifetime. Write commands that run from another process fail while the lock is held:

```
$ wacli chats mark-read --chat <jid> --json
{"success":false,"data":null,"error":"store is locked (another wacli is running?):
 store locked: resource temporarily unavailable (pid=30042 ...)"}
```

`--lock-wait` does not help. The follow process never releases the lock, so the wait always times out.

### What already works

The send delegate socket (`send_ipc.go`) solves this problem for sends. When `wacli send` hits a held lock, it asks the follow process to send on its behalf. The delegated kinds are `text`, `file`, `voice`, `sticker`, `react`, `location`, `poll`, `poll_vote`, `button_list_select`, `presence`, and `edit`.

`chats mark-read` is not a delegated kind. It is the only read-state write that a client next to a follow process needs, and it is the only one that cannot run.

### Request

Add `mark_read` as a delegated kind. When `wacli chats mark-read` hits a held lock, delegate the call to the follow process, as `wacli send` does.

### Use case

A terminal client keeps `wacli sync --follow` running for live messages, and shells out to `wacli` for actions. Sends and reactions work through the delegate. Mark-read is the one action that fails, so the client cannot mirror the read state back to WhatsApp while it runs.

Tested on wacli 0.16.0. The 0.17.x changelog does not mention mark-read delegation.
